newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan de-mining programme running out of money.
newsitem.headline: Afghan de-mining programme running out of money.

text.p: The United Nations is running out of money for its programme to clear the 10 million mines strewn across Afghanistan, according to a U.N. document.
The project only has enough money to continue until the middle of September.

"The mine action plan for Afghanistan is in a financial crisis. There are only enough funds available to ensure funding for teams until about mid-September, after which mine action staff will be suspended or asked to work voluntarily," according to the United Nations Weekly Update issued in Kabul.
Afghanistan has one of the world's worst land mine problems, a legacy of almost 20 years of continuous war.

The effects of the mines are gruesome. The U.N. estimates that 20 to 25 Afghans are injured by landmines each day, over 80 percent of them civilians. They say that some 400,000 people have been maimed by what the Red Cross has described as "the greatest violators of international humanitarian law".
The U.N. appealed for $22 million for its demining programme for 1997. According to the latest figures, less than half that amount has been pledged so far.

Even in areas of Afghanistan that are not affected by the continuing conflict, mines are preventing a return to normality. One of the demining programme's priorities is to clear villages so that some of the more than two million Afghans who are refugees can return.
"If we have to close down we will not be able to declare some areas safe for returnees," said Abdul Latif, acting officer in charge of the demining programme on Sunday.

The process of demining is slow. In the first six months of the year some 5.5 square miles (14.2 square km) of a total of almost 200 square miles (500 square km) affected by mines and unexploded ammunition had been cleared.
"The last week has been one of the worst ever for the mine clearance programme. In Kabul city alone, three men were killed and two others seriously injured while demining." says the Weekly Update.
"One man was killed by a booby trap and another two when they were trying to clear bushes in a minefield so that they could use their metal detectors." said Latif.
